entries.reason: Tolerance counted in rounds of upstream's 1 Hz health history (TargetUpdater.TimeToKillUpdateIntervalMs): two missed rounds before a forecast counts as stale. A cadence of the plugin's own sampling; the exact test 'filed in the latest round' would still need a bound for when sampling stops (A340).
Weight of the TTK self-correction's moving average (a sample counts a quarter), so one spike does not take over; it sets how fast the bias learns, not what it learns. No figure of the game (A340).

Upstream's intake criterion: a set that hits every counted member marks a party-wide hit only in a party of at least a light party; the smallest party composition in the game is 4 (ContentMemberType row 2: one tank, one healer, one melee, one ranged). Below it a cleave or a small circle can hit everyone. Deriving it from the current duty's composition would only raise the minimum where every member must be hit anyway

The game's battle NPC sub kind of a boss's invisible helpers, read from the object as a byte and compared; FFXIVClientStructs names no member for it, BossModReborn calls it Helper (ActorType 0x20B). A kind of the game, not a tunable
Percent to share: the effect text states the slow in percent and the reader needs a share; the divisor is the definition of the unit, as for the trait texts (A290, A340).

Length of the party's own health history in samples of the 1 Hz sampling (four minutes), upstream's former figure, fork-owned since upstream 3c6ce9ee2 removed the history. The readers measure from a member's first sample below full, so the bound only reaches a member never at full for four minutes; the TTK self-correction (ScoreTtkForecast, GetCorrectedTTK) measures what an old trend costs and divides it out. A memory length of the plugin, no figure of the game (A341).

entries.code: private static readonly TimeSpan CheckSpan = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(2.5);
entries.reason: Least span of a member's fall before a trend is read: three samples of the 1 Hz history, the same minimum upstream's TimeToKillTracker sets (MinSamples = 3); with two, one hit would be read as a rate. Upstream's former figure, fork-owned since 3c6ce9ee2. A statistical guard of the plugin's own estimate, no figure of the game; a GCD would match it only by chance (A341).

Smoothing of the trend's end point over the latest five samples, so one hit moves it by a fifth. Upstream's former figure, fork-owned since 3c6ce9ee2. The lag it brings on a steady fall makes the forecast late, which the TTK self-correction measures and divides out. No figure of the game (A341).

entries.code: var rest = TryStated(actionId, StatedFalloff, out var falloff) ? first * (1f - (falloff / 100f)) : first;
entries.reason: Unit conversion, not a game value: the tooltip states the falloff in percent ("30% less for all remaining enemies"), the potency of a further enemy is the share left (A342, A344).

The setting's own condition, "Experimental Pot Usage(used up to 5 seconds before SerpentsIre comes off cooldown)": a span named by the option text, not a tunable; it replaces the elapsed 115 s of the 120 s recast, which left out the time Serpent's Ire stands ready (A343).

Default AoE count of Hellfrog Medium and Deathfrog Medium, the least that lets the potency comparison speak: on two enemies 250 (400) each out-damages Bhavacakra's 400 (Zesho Meppo's 700) at level 100 (job guide, 7.5). The decision above it is HellfrogOutdamagesBhavacakra, read from the tooltips; the count stays his setting's lower bound (A345).

How long before the pull a melee presses its target dash: The Balance's Viper opener (Slither at -0.5 s, patch 7.55) and upstream's Thunderclap (<= 0.5 s, 33e6acb1f). No game sheet gives the time between pressing a dash and the character moving, nor the run speed, so nothing to derive it from; the model (melee_gapcloser_model.py) shows the first weaponskill lands 0-0.4 s after the pull across 0.5-0.9 s of animation lock (A347).
